Working on SimSurvey

Purpose and architecture

SimSurvey compares sampling designs against known, spatially correlated, age-structured populations. Keep the population process, sampling process, and estimation of population characteristics distinguishable. Preserve the ability to compare estimates with the corresponding truth.

The main workflow is sim_abundance() |> sim_distribution() |> sim_survey() |> run_strat() |> strat_error(). Functions accept and extend a named simulation list. Preserve existing components and their meanings when adding a stage; do not silently replace survey outputs with another data source.

Configurable closures are intentional public extension points. Recruitment, mortality, growth, spatial effects, catchability, and analysis functions can be supplied by users. Prefer small, composable functions to hard-coded biological relationships. Document the inputs and outputs required from a custom function. See vignettes/custom_closures.Rmd and Regular et al. (2020), https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0232822.

R conventions

  • Follow the surrounding style: two-space indentation, <-, double-quoted strings, snake_case function/argument names, and aligned wrapped arguments. Retain established scientific names such as N, R, Z, and N0.
  • Use the native |> pipe; the supported R version starts at 4.1.0. Historical analyses may still use older APIs or %>%; do not copy those conventions into new package code or reformat unrelated files.
  • Use the existing data.table, sf, and stars representations. Avoid adding another manipulation or spatial framework without a specific reason.
  • Internal helpers commonly start with .. Use namespace-qualified calls for optional packages, guard them with requireNamespace(), and give an actionable error when unavailable. Keep optional features out of the required core path.
  • Follow nearby data.table conventions, including local NULL declarations for non-standard evaluation where needed by package checks. Use data.table::copy() when new code would otherwise modify shared input tables by reference; check that repeated scenarios do not contaminate one another.
  • Do not set hidden seeds, register persistent global options, or change the user’s working directory in simulation functions. Clean up resources created by new code, including temporary files and parallel clusters, on error as well as success.

Scientific and data contracts

  • Preserve age/year matrix dimensions and dimnames, cell/set identifiers, and alignment between arrays, tables, and grids. Do not rely on incidental row order after joins. Keep dimensions when subsetting matrices and arrays.
  • Check conservation where appropriate: distributing abundance across cells or converting age to length must preserve totals. Rounding changes the population represented by round_sim(); its returned summaries must match its cells.
  • State units and distinguish abundance, density, catch, biomass, probabilities, and instantaneous rates. Grid distances/areas and fishing dimensions must use compatible units. Do not infer kilograms from counts without a weight model.
  • Preserve the package’s DFO length-group labels and consistent length groups between simulated truth, samples, age-length keys, and stratified analyses.
  • Validate documented domains and dimensions with informative errors. Test mathematical behavior independently rather than copying implementation code.
  • Keep scientific model changes explicit. A failing test is not permission to redesign mortality, movement, selectivity, or an estimator. Fix clear defects narrowly and record broader questions for discussion.

Documentation and repository layout

  • Edit roxygen comments in R/ for function documentation. Include assumptions, argument and output meanings, units, extension contracts, and small examples. Regenerate the affected man/ files and NAMESPACE with roxygen2; do not hand edit generated documentation. Avoid unrelated generator/version churn.
  • Record user-visible changes and bug fixes in NEWS.md. Keep development versions distinct from releases; current work toward 0.2.0 uses 0.1.8.9000.
  • Verify vignette resources inside the built source archive, not only a local render. Embed generated local widget resources because R cleans their support directories; explicitly mark web-loaded scripts external to avoid build downloads.
  • Keep research analyses, exploratory scripts, and large simulations under analysis/ (excluded from builds). The archived informal tests are historical examples, not the automated test suite. data-raw/ contains data preparation; do not replace bundled data without a reproducible preparation change.
  • Do not commit local R libraries, check/build results, credentials, or generated research outputs. Keep changes focused and preserve existing user work.

Tests and checks

The automated suite uses testthat edition 3 in tests/testthat/.

  • Run testthat::test_local() during development. Use tiny local fixtures and withr::local_seed() for stochastic tests; reset each test’s RNG explicitly.
  • Prefer analytical expectations, conservation, dimensions, sampling bounds, documented errors/warnings, and same-seed reproducibility to large snapshots or fragile Monte Carlo thresholds. Include zero catch and sampling boundaries when changing sampling code.
  • Tests must not access the network, launch interactive displays, write outside temporary directories, or require INLA for the core simulation workflow. Explicitly skip optional-feature tests when their dependencies are absent.
  • Test behavior changes and add a regression test for each defect fix. Exercise custom closures as well as defaults. Do not equate equal seeds with identical random results across serial and parallel implementations.
  • Before considering work complete, build the source package and run R CMD check --no-manual on it. Confirm that tests/testthat.R is included and executed. The GitHub Actions matrix checks Windows, macOS, and multiple R versions. Report the checks actually run and any remaining warnings or skips.

Fisheries development

Fisheries attribute existing total mortality to fishing; they do not subtract deaths again from future pre-generated populations. Keep stock and catch tables aggregate, with exact whole-fish mortality conservation. Complete all fishing truth before monitoring so monitoring controls cannot alter fishing outcomes. Keep effort units explicit and distinguish true catches from reported estimates. Weight and maturity belong to the population. Refresh B and S from the joint length-age key when abundance changes; do not substitute weight at mean length or multiply separately averaged weight and maturity. S is all-fish expected mature biomass, without spawning timing or sex structure. Complete every existing sample before maturity draws, and draw latent maturity for every measured fish before applying observation masks. Preserve the established sim_length component. Batch functions take sim first and named configurations thereafter. Declare all fisheries and their user-supplied allocations upfront, interleave operations on one stock/budget, and generate survey-program truth independently before biological subsampling. Use only the current year’s spatial population when initializing fishery stocks; test starting ledger counts against that year’s cells, not just ledger balance. Keep survey_programs separate from the surveys scenario-design table, and restore matching spatial availability when extracting a survey for analysis. See vignettes/fisheries.Rmd for the implemented model and limitations; analysis/fisheries-design.Rmd remains a historical research note.
